content: Launched in 2014 as a program of the Stamford Peace Youth Foundation, the Beyond Limits Academic Program provides highly subsidized one-on-one tutoring and informal mentoring to students attending Stamford Public Schools and other schools in lower Fairfield County. Tutoring is typically conducted by upperclassmen, many of whom are referred by teachers, administrators and other tutors. We also have a number of college students around the world working with us. Tutoring sessions are held at our headquarters on Long Ridge Road, which includes dedicated tutoring rooms equipped with chromebooks, school supplies, and other program materials, a lounge area with Wi-Fi for families, a kitchen with water and snacks, and academic reference books. Please click HERE to view our most recent program highlights.
To create an equitable academic ecosystem in lower Fairfield County and beyond by empowering every learner through tutoring, informal mentoring, advocacy, and collaboration with local partners.

Beyond Limits' mission is to level the academic playing field and eliminate opportunity gaps for learners in lower Fairfield County. We empower every learner to achieve their potential through high-quality, subsidized, non-school-based peer-to-peer tutoring, mentoring, academic advocacy, and enrichment activities. By collaborating with local partners, we create a sustainable, inclusive academic support network that fosters a thirst for knowledge and equitable access to opportunities.

We are so grateful for the grant we recently received from the New Canaan Community Foundation. The NCCF addresses community needs by providing leadership on local issues, making impactful grants, and facilitating effective charitable giving.
Thank you for all that you do to support non-profits in our community!
We are pleased to receive the continued support of Near & Far Aid and are grateful for all that you do!
Emily Gordon and Suzanne Jesse | Co-Presidents

Near & Far Aid is an all-volunteer fundraising and fund-granting organization that makes a positive impact on thousands of people in Fairfield County by granting over $1 million a year to well-vetted local agencies addressing poverty and changing lives.
EQUITY through access: Providing accessible, discounted, high-quality academic supports to bridge the opportunity gap among all participants
EMPOWERMENT through support: Fostering confidence through personalized tutoring, enrichment programming and informal mentoring to help students reach their full potential.

COMMUNITY through collaboration: Building a support network among students, families, tutors and other community organizations to create a broad and supportive learning environment that drives success.

This scholarship is awarded to students in honor of Bill Susetka's memory. Bill graduated from Stamford Catholic High School. He was accomplished in athletics, having played on the Stamford World Champion Babe Ruth baseball team and the varsity baseball and basketball teams at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute. Still, he remained humble and reveled in other’s triumphs. Bill was an inspirational leader with a kind, compassionate, and generous nature, who cared deeply about people and always had a smile and encouraging words to share. To honor his memory, the friends and family of Bill Susetka have established this scholarship for worthy Stamford Peace student-athletes. The successful candidate is in good academic standing, displays good citizenship, and demonstrates financial need.

We provide Individualized academic tutoring in math & science – generally two 1-hour sessions per week per participant, available on weekday afternoons and evenings and Saturdays on a personalized schedule.

Tutoring is conducted “peer-to-peer”, i.e., our tutors are high-achieving local high school juniors, seniors, and local college students assigned to 4th thru 10th graders. Tutors and tutees rotate, with pairings based upon our assessment of current best “fit.”
Tutoring sessions can take place in person in our tutoring center or remotely via Zoom, which can allow for greater flexibility and convenience.
Tutoring fees are on a sliding scale and are substantially subsidized for families eligible to receive discounted services (formerly free or reduced-price school lunch).
Our approach also offers valuable informal mentoring benefits.
To learn more and apply, follow the QR code on our recruitment flyer BELOW.

Our elite-level AAU basketball program, with teams for boys and girls in the 3rd through 11th grades. Tryout based, teams are both competitive and very selective. Each team plays between 5-12 tournaments per season (depending upon grade and level of play) throughout the Northeast region and elsewhere. Tryouts for our AAU teams take place towards the end of the winter season.

The Stamford Peace Boys Basketball League, a local winter developmental league (available without regard to basketball ability or experience) for elementary and middle school boys. This league generally runs from mid-November through early March. Teams practice one weekday per week, followed by an either Saturday or Sunday game. Every team earns a berth in a single-elimination playoff/championship tournament.

Peace Basketball Summer League, as a program of J Basketball is a summer league (available without regard to basketball ability or experience) for middle school boys and high school boys. This league runs from the July timeframe through mid-August. All teams have 2 games games per weekend and concludes with a two day-single tournament.

Stamford Peace was founded in 2008 by long-time Stamford community member and current Notre Dame Prep of Sacred Heart University Boys Varsity basketball coach, Brian Kriftcher, following a successful 20-year career in financial services. At the age of 40, Brian retired from business to devote his full-time energies to his “calling” for coaching, teaching, and community development. Brian and fellow coach and Stamford community member, Lenwood Latta, developed Stamford Peace as a direct response to what they perceived was a systemic problem in which relatively low academic priorities and inadequate support were preventing too many local student-athletes from achieving their full potential. From a single team of 9-10-year-old boys in 2008, Stamford Peace has grown to more than 1,200 young people today across a variety of basketball activities and academic support programs. Our focus on Sports, Academics, and Citizenship is supported by two key pillars: PEACE Basketball, and our Beyond Limits Academic Program.

PEACE Basketball is dedicated to the philosophy that “basketball is a privilege” – representing a reward for consistent effort and achievement in children’s core responsibilities in the classroom, in the community, and at home. PEACE Basketball offers a first-rate basketball educational experience emphasizing the development of strong fundamentals and high-quality competition, as well as establishing a culture of excellence among our players and in our overall approach to the game. Among our PEACE Basketball offerings are a boys' winter house basketball league; over a dozen elite-level boys' and girls' travel AAU basketball teams; summer and vacation day basketball camps; a summer league; year-round clinics and open gym activities; and individual training. Stamford Peace is built on a foundation consisting of teamwork, discipline, leadership, and sportsmanship. Rather than focusing exclusively on wins and losses, the goal of Stamford Peace includes using the game of basketball as a vehicle through which to positively influence academic achievement, community service, and other life skills within Stamford and other lower Fairfield County communities.

To that end, in 2013 we launched our Beyond Limits Academic Program initially as a tool to support student-athletes, but Beyond Limits has expanded considerably, such that today we support far more non-athlete students than athletes, and focus almost exclusively on economically disadvantaged and underserved students. Beyond Limits employs a peer-to-peer approach, in which local high school students provide one-on-one academic tutoring, primarily in math and science, to other local middle school and high school students. Fees are highly subsidized by Stamford Peace. In addition to regular tutoring, our Beyond Limits program conducts periodic workshops and other enrichment activities covering such topics as financial literacy, standardized test preparation, college planning and others. Throughout each of these academic activities, we actively partner with parents, teachers, and administrators as important shared advocates for our participants.

Stamford Peace Youth Foundation uses high level basketball instruction, training, and competition as well as academic support, to positively influence young people and help them achieve their full potential on and off the court.

Stamford Peace Youth Foundation, a 501c3 not-for-profit corporation founded in 2008, is dedicated to the philosophy that “basketball is a privilege,” through which it actively encourages consistent effort and achievement in children’s core responsibilities in the classroom, in the community and at home.

We started Stamford Peace in 2008 with great purpose around a name and mission that brings people together. We believe deeply in PEACE as not the absence of war, but the development of connection and valuing our differences. Basketball and Academic supports are merely the tools by which we perpetually try to lift people up to the level of their potential, without regard to race, gender, religion, ethnicity, sexual orientation, or otherwise. Our diversity is and remains our society’s and local community’s crown jewel.

We are cognizant of the fact that our society’s full promise has eluded too many for far too long. The issue of racial division and other inequities in America requires active, open, honest, direct, and respectful encounters to overcome them. As we face a crossroads – do we truly come together or do we remain apart? -- Stamford Peace remains wholly committed to doing all we can to champion justice and to play a leadership role in supporting our community’s most underserved; to combat all forms of racism and bigotry; and to be a vocal ally in the ongoing struggle for a more fair, loving and inclusive world.

Stamford Peace does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin (ancestry), religion, gender identity (including gender expression), sexual orientation, disability, age, marital status, family/parental status, military status or any other characteristic protected by law in any of its activities, programs or operations, including employment.

content: Our growth and success over the years — measured and evaluated based upon data as well as testimonials — reflects the perceived value of our unique peer-to-peer academic support model. Of course, we believe much of that has to do with the quality of our delivery – including the care with which we match students with tutors; our tutors’ knowledge and experience level; the affordability and flexible timing of our tutoring sessions; and other internal factors. Externally, it is also a function of the huge demand for affordable academic support services particularly for lower income youth.

Juana is a 7th grader who has been attending Beyond Limits for 2 years. She first came to BL to improve her math skills but also takes advantage of enrichment programs, like coding classes and writing workships. She credits her BL tutors with helping her overcome her doubts in math and giving her all the tools she needs to solve math problems. For students considering BL, she says: "Take this opportunity because it will help you alot. You learn every time you go. And by personal experience, I highly recommend it."

Matthew came to Beyond Limits as a freshman when he was having trouble in math. Now a senior, he says the program helped him grow, gain more confidence and improve in multiple subjects. For students considering BL, Matthew tells them: "You should definitely come. The tutors here are competent and will offer you academic help as well as support from their own experiences. Beyond Limits helps tons of kids every week."

content: We emphasize to our players that the game – and the accompanying "investments" by parents, coaches and other mentors in their success – is neither a "given" nor an "end" in and of itself. Rather, playing is the ongoing reward for our players' pursuit of excellence in their core responsibilities in the classroom, in the community, and at home. We encourage our players to “use basketball, rather than to allow basketball to use them,” a principal mantra by which we drive student-athletes to appropriately prioritize their academics and other life skills.

Following a successful 18-year Wall Street career, Brian Kriftcher (Coach "K”) retired from the business world at the age of 40 in order to devote his full-time energies to his passions for coaching, teaching and philanthropic work.

Coach "K" is the Founder and President of Stamford Peace Youth Foundation; and is Head Coach of PEACE Basketball. He Is an experienced high school basketball coach at Westhill High School in Stamford, CT, as well as at St. Luke's School in New Canaan, CT. At St. Luke's, Coach K led his Varsity boys' basketball team to a coveted Fairchester Athletic Association tournament crown, before losing in the Championship game of the New England Preparatory School Athletic Conference tournament in 2010–2011.

Coach "K" has been a lifelong student and teacher of the game, and has successfully coached both boys’ and girls’ teams representing Stamford in several JCC Maccabi Games, as well as many other teams in many other events. Coach "K" has worked at such distinguished basketball camps as the Bob Hurley Basketball Camp, Coach K Academy/Duke Basketball Camp, and Point Guard College. He is also a frequent basketball clinician/instructor and 1-on-1 trainer.

As a player, Coach K earned a Silver Medal representing the U.S.A. as a member of its Masters (35+ years old) basketball team in the World Maccabiah Games in Israel in 2009. Previously, he earned a Gold Medal in the Pan American Maccabiah Games in Buenos Aires, Argentina in 2007.

Coach "K" earned his Bachelor of Arts degree in Political Science from the State University of New York at Albany, where he was member of the men’s intercollegiate basketball team for two seasons. He earned a law degree from St. John’s University Law School, which he attended at night; and remains licensed to practice law in New York State.

Coach "K" is the Global Chairman of the Board of Directors of PeacePlayers International; a not-for-profit organization that uses the game of basketball to bridge divides between young people in conflict areas throughout the world. From 2009 – 2012, he was president of the Stamford JCC.
Coach "K" has been a Stamford resident since 1996, where he lives with his wife, Jeannie, and three daughters, Hannah, Charlotte and Sophie
In 2013, Andy Sklover co-founded the Beyond Limits Academic Program as a program of Stamford Peace Basketball Club, Inc.

As a former member of the City of Stamford’s Board of Representatives (BOR), he served as chair of the Education Committee and a member of the Fiscal, State & Commerce and Charter Review Committees. As Education Committee Chair, he lead the establishment of the BOR’s Student Advisory Council (SAC), which seeks to empower the Stamford Public School (SPS) student body by granting student representatives an opportunity to express their thoughts and opinions and favorably impact the current and future academic and social experiences of SPS students. He has also served as a member of a School Governance Council and the High School Call to Action and District Technology Committees.

From December, 2012 to June, 2015, Sklover served, on a part-time basis, as Director of Advocacy and Education for Stamford Achieves, a non-profit established in 2004 to serve as an advocate and catalyst for closing the achievement gap in Stamford.

He earned his Bachelor of Arts degree in Economics from Northwestern University and an MBA from Columbia University. He is the President of Sklover Benefits Group, Inc., an insurance brokerage firm also based in Stamford.
A resident of Stamford since 2001 with his wife, Lauren, and his two daughters – Marley and Ryan – who have both attended Stamford Public Schools since kindergarten

Bill Susetka was a student-athlete at Stamford's Catholic High School and later at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute, playing basketball and baseball. The KHBA’s mission is to educate, empower, and inspire young people in Kosovo using the game of basketball as a tool to develop their love for the game; their skills and talents; and their dreams and opportunities for a brighter future. The idea is to grow a community of leaders through more advanced coaching and mentorship that will enrich each participant’s athletic skills and leadership capabilities, and further their education through basketball. Through these efforts, we hope to enhance the quality and reach of Kosovo basketball for the long-term.
Please make your donation to the Kosovo Heritage Basketball Academy HERE - and select "KHBA" from the CAMPAIGN drop down box.
